text:
Sam: heads up — us-west-2 spot churn spiked at 02:12 UTC, ~18% eviction rate across g5 pools. Several mid-tier customers saw degraded p99s and a handful of requests fell back to cpu-hosts. :warning:
Nora: saw the alerts. Which queues exactly? any model skew (long ctx vs short)?
Luis: primarily long-context chat lanes (>=2048) on mixed g5/preemptible pools. Short gen lanes mostly ok.
Priya: that explains it — different preemption sensitivity because long ctx holds KV cache and keeps workers pinned longer.
Sam: confirmed. Eviction bursts coincide with a preemptible capacity reclaim window in that region. Cloud reported a maintenance event + spot demand surge.
Marco: I think we should avoid full cross-region fanout as the first step — cold KV cache will blow latency even worse. Propose tiered fallback:
- Tier A (enterprise): failover to regional dedicated capacity (if available), else model-variant fallback (quantized or lower-temp) in-region.
- Tier B (paid/self-serve): model-variant fallback in-region, then limited cross-region spill (max 10% of requests).
- Tier C (free/canary): immediate spill to cheapest preemptible/CPU pools with lower p99 SLOs.
Nora: +1. Also we should add a safety cap on cross-region concurrent inflight to avoid bursting remote infra. Maybe implement token-bucket per-src-region.
Luis: also need to adjust routing policy weights on churn signal so we prefer dedicated/different instance types before region exit.
Priya: for model-variant fallback, suggestion: prefer int8 quantized variant with same architecture; keep a fast fallback path that preserves response shape (no format shifts).
Sam: example pseudo policy (very rough):
```yaml
on_eviction: route -> preferred_pool
on_eviction_weight: 1.0
on_eviction_fanout: 1
on_eviction_model_variant: full_fp16
eviction_detected:
  - try: regional_dedicated (capacity_quota > 0)
  - try: regional_preemptible_variant (variant=int8, max_inflight=0.3)
  - try: cross_region_spill (limit=0.1, token_bucket)
  - else: cpu_fallback
```
Marco: we should also tie this to customer_tier metadata in the routing decision — keep enterprise on dedicated longer.
capacity-bot: FYI: us-west-2 preemptible pool g5-16 currently at 78% utilization; ded pool has 12 spare GPUs.
Sam: action items I propose:
1) Implement a soft cap on cross-region fanout (token bucket) — short patch to routing service (Luis + Marco)
2) Add model-variant tag and quick fallthrough path preserving response schema (Priya)
3) Short-term: bump enterprise routing weight to prefer ded (Ops)
4) Ops: request cloud provider for preemptible stability details and ETA for maintenance end (Sam + Nora)
Nora: I'll take 4. Also will add a short dashboard panel for eviction rate per pool and per-tenant impact so we can watch spill rates.
Luis: I'll start the token-bucket PR and a simulation to validate p99 change when limiting fanout to 10%.
Priya: I'll prepare the quantized variant rollout checklist — we need canary prompts and evals to ensure no regression.
Marco: agree on staged rollout. Can we also add a fallback TTL so requests don't keep bouncing between regions? e.g., once spilled, mark request trace with region_fallback:true for 60s.
Sam: good call. Prevents oscillation.
ops-bot: heads-up — will throttle non-critical restarts during maintenance window.
Sam: timeline: start implementation today for token-bucket + routing weight change, monitor next 6 hours. If eviction persists beyond 3 hours, trigger emergency cross-region capacity (manual).
Nora: :thumbsup: I'll post a short note to #incidents if we hit the 3-hour threshold.
Marco: one more thought — consider ephemeral 'prewarm' workers that accept only warm-cache handoffs during surge; cheaper than full ded but reduce cold-cache spike. Worth prototyping later.
Sam: noted. Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene in 2h for status. :clock2:
